name: OmniQEC
reason: arXiv abs page verified: 'OmniQEC: discovering practical quantum error-correcting codes by an AI scientist' (arXiv:2607.25865, v1 submitted 2026-07-28, Yan et al., not withdrawn). LLM-orchestrated dual-loop discovery system (fast code-level screening plus slow circuit-level validation) that found hardware-friendly QEC codes outperforming established baselines at fixed physical-qubit budgets - genuine multi-step in-silico scientific discovery. No code or data link on the abs page, so paper-only. Category physics (quantum computing); autonomy A3 (in-silico closed loop; simulation closure is not A5).

record.name: OmniQEC
record.inputs: QEC code-family search spaces, hardware constraints and physical-qubit budgets; LLM backends
record.outputs: Candidate quantum error-correcting codes with code-level screening metrics and circuit-level decoder validation
record.notes: AI-scientist system in which an LLM orchestrator coordinates a dual-loop workflow - fast screening on code-level metrics and slow circuit-level validation (syndrome extraction, decoder evaluation) - discovering hardware-friendly codes that outperform established baselines at given qubit budgets. No code released as of verification (2026-08-13); fully in-silico, human-launched runs.

name: Autonomous Research Agents: A Survey of AI Scientists and the Verification Gap
reason: Confirmed survey, not a system or benchmark harness. arXiv abs page verified (arXiv:2608.05179, submitted 2026-06-29, Ding et al., not withdrawn): codes 35 autonomous-research-agent works across lifecycle/auditability dimensions and proposes a reporting checklist, but the page links no code repository, harness, dataset download, or project site - the 'coded corpus' and checklist have no released artifact. Pre-adjudicated reject confirmed: offers no released harness, so it fails the scope gate (the catalog is not a list of surveys).
